summary: Iteration 7 — Lily AI concierge fully tested (backend + frontend). All 12 pytest cases pass. Widget shows Lily header, avatar, TTS toggle, handoff button, options bubble with 4 buttons that trigger /lily/reply. Dashboard shows emotion badge and CustomerMemoryPanel with 来访次数 / past issues / complaint count / emotion distribution. Admin toggle correctly disables Lily. Emotion detection returned 'angry' with confidence 0.95 and an apology-first reply; escalate=true on '我要转人工'; WS emotion_update broadcast verified live to agent websocket.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/lily.py:handoff — imports route_new_session/agent_active_count/clean_session inside function; consider top-level for readability but not blocking.

lily_service.py:_call_llm swallows all exceptions and returns empty string, which triggers a fallback reply. This masks LLM outages — consider logging failure count/emitting metric so operators notice provider-side incidents.
chat.py session-creation rate limit (5/hr per IP) is aggressive for shared preview/prod IPs; conftest already purges 127.0.0.1 to work around this. Non-blocking, but worth documenting for e2e users.
seed_data_creation: Test file creates TEST_lily_* / TEST_dash_* prefixed customer sessions; conftest purges IP-based session records before each test to bypass 5/hr rate limit.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Rate limit 5/hr per IP on /api/chat/session is real; purge db.sessions by customer_ip before mass e2e runs. LLM (Claude Sonnet 4.6 via Emergent key) is live and returns valid JSON per LILY_SYSTEM prompt — emotion detection classifies '你们太慢了/太差了/生气' as 'angry' with confidence > 0.9. Frontend Lily header only shows in Lily phase (after prechat submit); after handoff or when disabled globally, widget skips straight to human queue.
rca of the issue: No unresolved issues. Initial pytest failures were payload-schema drift in the test script (chat.SessionCreate uses name/email/subject, not customer_name/customer_email/initial_message) — fixed in test file.
